Contracted sockets: scleral graft transplantation

Among 39 patients, the LLLT group had faster graft vascularization and less fornix contraction than controls. The primary paper is a retrospective chart review; detailed methods assign groups by whether patients accepted additional LLLT, despite the abstract phrase “randomly enrolled.” Blinding is not described.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Among 39 patients, the LLLT group had faster graft vascularization and less fornix contraction than controls. The primary paper is a retrospective chart review; detailed methods assign groups by whether patients accepted additional LLLT, despite the abstract phrase “randomly enrolled.” Blinding is not described.

Summary of the Evidence

One unique 2023 clinical publication compares adjunctive LLLT with no LLLT after scleral graft transplantation in 39 patients. The primary article describes a retrospective chart review from 2015 to 2021. Although the abstract says patients were randomly enrolled, the detailed methods state that patients who accepted additional LLLT entered the laser group and those who refused were controls. Allocation therefore followed treatment acceptance, and blinding is not described. The database field labels the study randomized and double-blind, which is not supported by the methods reported in the article. A 2021 same-center 10-patient postoperative series concerns a similar procedure, and participant overlap cannot be excluded; it is described in the conjunctival-sac-stenosis category rather than counted as an independent trial here.

Human and clinical evidence

Huang and colleagues compared 18 patients receiving LLLT with 21 controls. The article reported faster graft vascularization in the LLLT group and less fornix contraction at follow-up, including three and six months. This is a retrospective comparison, not a clearly documented randomized, blinded trial. The methods indicate that treatment acceptance determined group assignment, while the abstract's phrase “randomly enrolled” does not provide a randomization method (Huang et al. 2023 DOI 10.1186/s12886-023-03242-3, Article).

Animal evidence

No separate animal study was identified within this exact category. The rabbit component of the 2021 related publication is counted under conjunctival sac stenosis and does not represent another publication here.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone cell or tissue study was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The article reports a 650 nm red laser, 10 mW output with a stated 0–20 mW range, 3.8 J/cm², and 12.7 mW/cm² irradiance with a 10 mm spot at 1 cm. Treatment was five minutes daily for seven days, beginning one week after surgery. These parameters apply to LLLT after scleral graft transplantation. Similarity to the earlier same-center protocol raises possible overlap and limits the interpretation of the reports as independent replications.

Interpretation

The retrospective comparison reports better vascularization and less contraction with adjunctive LLLT. The design classification in the database is erroneous: the source describes retrospective comparison and does not document randomization or blinding. Selection, overlap, and lack of independent replication limit causal confidence.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The study is a 39-person retrospective comparison. Its abstract says patients were randomly enrolled, but methods state that those who accepted LLLT entered the laser group and those who refused were controls. This acceptance-based allocation and absent blinding weaken causal confidence. The existing database incorrectly calls it randomized and double-blind; independent prospective replication would help.
